title: Criminal Law vs. Civil Law
text: Criminal law deals with offenses against the state or society (such as theft or assault), prosecuted by government authorities, with penalties including fines or imprisonment. Civil law deals with disputes between private parties (such as contract breaches or personal injury claims), typically resulting in monetary compensation or specific remedies rather than criminal punishment. The standard of proof is generally higher in criminal cases ('beyond a reasonable doubt') than in civil cases ('preponderance of the evidence').
